text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers.

- UMNO leaders vying for posts in October's party elections will be disqualified or expelled if they are found engaging in money politics or other unethical practices to boost their election standings, said Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.

- Malaysia will continue to give priority to programmes aimed at enhancing economic growth in the 1997 Budget, but will not neglect its responsibilities of eradicating poverty and combating social ills, said Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.

- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad appoints new Chief Secretary to the Government, Halim Abdul Ali. The premier expressed hope Halim will strengthen co-operation between civil service and private sector. Halim replaces retiring Ahmad Sarji Abdul Hamid.
- Central bank Bank Negara will soon implement a merit/demerit system for insurance companies to bring about changes and improvements in the industry.
- Regulated short selling on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange will start on September 30, the exchange announced.

- Expatriate managers and professionals earn much more than Malaysian executives of similar ranking, a recent survey released by Bank Negara showed. The bank indicated the trend was expected to continue into this year.
- A full cabinet reshuffle of the Sarawak state government will be made early next year, said Chief Minister Abdul Taib Mahmud.
- Leader Universal Holdings, vying for a greater share of the Asian telecommunications and power sectors, expects to conclude a deal to acquire an Indian listed company before the year-end.
